newsitem.title: USA: Brent talk heats up in US Gulf, buyers stay cool.
newsitem.headline: Brent talk heats up in US Gulf, buyers stay cool.

text.p: A half dozen companies were gauging U.S. interest in North Sea Brent crude oil on Wednesday, but buyers remained cool for the moment, traders said.
The benchmark grade was offered at parity to September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing for September 5-10 arrival. Later arrivals were heard offered at five to 15 cents discount, traders said.
A week ago, the asking price was around 25 cents under WTI/Cushing.
The increase reflected the steadily rising price of dated cargoes in Europe.
A European company on Wednesday sold a Brent cargo loading August 4-6 to another European company at August Brent plus 15 cents a barrel, up five cents from Tuesday and 10 cents from Monday.

The Brent offers seemed unusual in light of the still-narrow trans-Atlantic arbitrage. The September spread between WTI and Brent futures was around $1.15-1.20 a barrel just before the NYMEX closed on Wednesday.
Sellers, however, had nothing to lose in testing the market since prices are unlikely to get much higher, traders said.
"If you can get sales off at that level and then Iraq comes back in, Dated (Brent) is going to get dumped 20 cents," a Gulf Coast trader said.
Another trader said the market so far bore few alternatives in that first-half September timeframe.

In one of the first September foreign crude trades, a U.S. refiner on Tuesday picked up a Nigerian Bonny Light cargo from a trading house for September 6-10 delivery at Dated Brent plus $1.97 a barrel.
Bonny Light, Brass River and Qua Iboe for August delivery were heard to be still on offer at $1.90-2.00 over Dated Brent, although most refiners have wrapped up their month's requirements.
In Latin America, loadings of Colombian Cano Limon crude oil have been delayed by 10-20 days in July and August in the wake of the shutdown of Cano Limon operations.
Operations at the 175,000 barrel per day (bpd) field and on the pipeline to the Covenas terminal have returned to normal after recent back-to-back rebel attacks.
